headline: BeTH reuses the City's StreetSaver projections of the network average and sets beside them the measured condition distribution: 41.6% of the network below PCI 50 in the 2024 inspection. An average target is not a failed-streets target.
chain: network PCI over time (City deterioration model)

performance_assessment.question: What would it take to bring Berkeley pavement to PCI 60 or better, and what would that mean for the worst streets?

measure_1_network_average.what: Network-average PCI, the measure the City projects.
measure_1_network_average.reading: On the City's projections the Five-Year Plan alone falls to about 56 by 2038; adding Measure FF (about $29.6M a year, 12-year average) reaches about 62; reaching 70 by 2036 needs about $37.6M a year. These are averages over 213 centerline miles.
measure_1_network_average.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

measure_2_condition_distribution.what: How much of the network is below PCI 50 and below PCI 25 (MTC "failed"), the measure Measure FF's goal names: PCI 70 "ideally with no streets having a PCI below 50" by December 31, 2036.

now_2024_inspection.source: City of Berkeley 2024 Pavement Management Program Update (P-TAP Round 25), Pavement Engineering Inc., April 2025, Executive Summary pp.2-3 and Section IV street list; see phase2/data/network-condition.json

treated_by_adopted_plans_fy2027_2031.source: July 7, 2026 plan attachments, validated per year; phase2/data/street-plan-conditions.json

projected_2038.needed_from: StreetSaver output of the condition distribution (or miles below PCI 50) under each funding scenario. The Measure FF annual report must include "the PCI of all streets" (BMC 7.11.050(B)(1)).

performance_assessment.finding: Reaching a network average of 60, or even 62, is not the same as eliminating failed streets. In the 2024 inspection the average was 56 while 88.8 centerline miles (42%) were below PCI 50 and 34.0 miles (16%) were below 25. The two adopted plans treat 22.6 miles of currently-below-50 streets over FY2027-FY2031 (9.4 through Measure FF, 13.2 through the Five-Year Plan), while other streets deteriorate past 50. Whether the below-50 total shrinks is not shown by any published projection.
performance_assessment.tradeoff_the_city_published: Selecting Measure FF streets below PCI 50 instead of by cost-effectiveness lowers the 2038 network average by about one point (62 instead of 63) while treating the worst streets first (City Figure 2). The average and the distribution move in different directions.
performance_assessment.the_adopted_goal_is_70: Berkeley's goal is PCI 70 (BMC 7.11.010(K)(1)), not 60, paired with the below-50 condition. The City estimates PCI 70 by 2036 needs about $8M a year more than the Plan plus Measure FF.
critical_caveats: Scenario values are the City's projections. BeTH restates them; it cannot test them without the City's deterioration curves and treatment catalog.

The distribution is from 2024 inspections, before FY2025-FY2026 paving (about 18.7 centerline miles). Plan-attachment PCIs are the values printed in July 2026 and will be lower when streets are treated.
Annual investment figures are 12-year averages including revenue growth, not flat annual amounts.
Reaching a level and holding it are different problems with different funding profiles.

city_scenarios.label: Five-Year Plan baseline
city_scenarios.description: Only the funding in the proposed Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan. PCI falls from 59 to about 56 by 2038 as construction cost escalation outpaces revenue growth.
city_scenarios.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

city_scenarios.label: Five-Year Plan + Measure FF
city_scenarios.description: Adds Measure FF funding. PCI improves from 59 to about 62 by 2038. Measure FF accounts for the entire difference between this and the baseline.
city_scenarios.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

city_scenarios.label: Reach 70 by 2036, then maintain
city_scenarios.description: The investment level the City estimates is needed to reach PCI 70 by 2036 and hold it through 2038. About $8M a year more than the Plan and Measure FF currently provide.
city_scenarios.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

city_selection_methods.label: Critical Point (WER-driven)
city_selection_methods.description: Selects Measure FF streets using the same WER methodology as the Five-Year Plan.
city_selection_methods.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.13 (Figure 2, selection methods)

city_selection_methods.label: PCI Under 50 targeting
city_selection_methods.description: Targets streets below PCI 50, consistent with Measure FF's stated goal of addressing long-deferred repairs.
city_selection_methods.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.13 (Figure 2, selection methods)

marginal_cost_per_pci_point.derivation: BeTH arithmetic on two published City scenarios
marginal_cost_per_pci_point.caveat: Coarse. Non-linear relationship, 12-year endpoints, differing selection methods.

marginal_cost_per_pci_point.derivation: BeTH arithmetic on two published City scenarios
marginal_cost_per_pci_point.caveat: Coarse. Non-linear relationship, 12-year endpoints, differing selection methods.

current_network_pci.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.16 (Background)
current_network_pci.note: Citywide PCI cited by the City in July 2026. The 2024 inspection (PTAP-25) reports 56; the July 2026 plan starts its projections at 59 "after planned work" in 2026.

pci_after_fy2026_work.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, pp.11-12 (PCI projections, Figure 1)

assessment_cycle.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.8 (selection methods) and pp.11-12
assessment_cycle.note: PCI scored per street section from observed surface distresses, fed into StreetSaver.

adopted_goal.source: BMC 7.11.010(K)(1), Measure FF initiative text, PDF p.7 (phase2/sources/measure-ff-ordinance-transcription.md)
adopted_goal.note: Goal of citywide PCI 70 "ideally with no streets having a PCI below 50". Measure FF prioritises streets below PCI 50.

total_lane_miles.source: City of Berkeley 2024 Pavement Management Program Update (P-TAP Round 25), Pavement Engineering Inc., April 2025, Executive Summary pp.2-3 and Section IV street list; see phase2/data/network-condition.json
total_lane_miles.note: 212.77 centerline miles; 39,363,218 sq ft of pavement.

pci_distribution.source: City of Berkeley 2024 Pavement Management Program Update (P-TAP Round 25), Pavement Engineering Inc., April 2025, Executive Summary pp.2-3 and Section IV street list; see phase2/data/network-condition.json
pci_distribution.note: 1,216 street sections with 2024 PCI, validated to the report totals. 88.75 centerline miles (41.6%) below PCI 50; 33.99 miles (15.9%) below PCI 25. As of 2024 inspection, before FY2025-FY2026 paving.

deterioration.note: Deterioration is non-linear. Below roughly PCI 40 the required treatment escalates from surface seal to full reconstruction at several times the cost. A linear assumption makes PCI 60 look far cheaper to reach than it is, so no linear fallback is provided.

catalog.needed_from: StreetSaver treatment catalog: eligibility PCI band, unit cost per square foot, service life, post-treatment PCI

treatments.note: Treatment eligibility depends on current PCI. A treatment valid at PCI 70 is usually invalid at PCI 35.

cost_decomposition.needed_from: Contract bid tabs, broken into pavement treatment, design, construction management, ADA, utilities, drainage, traffic safety, environmental work, green infrastructure, discretionary scope

delivery_cost.note: Whether delivery reform frees real money can only be answered from this decomposition. Do not presume environmental review is the primary driver; that is the hypothesis to test.

measure_ff_fy2027_revenue.source: FY2027 adopted budget, Exhibit C p.254; FY2027 tax rate report p.1
measure_ff_fy2027_revenue.note: Approximately 45% is for streets by ordinance (BMC 7.11.020(C)); the adopted program puts 45.6% into street rehabilitation.

redirectable_from_capital.note: Measure FF: $0 more for paving without voters. CIP Fund 501: at most $2,946,000 of FY2027-28 appropriations, only by deferring every other fund 501 project; one-time carryover unknown. Other sources not yet researched.

construction_cost_pct_per_year.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12
construction_cost_pct_per_year.note: Reflects recent asphalt and paving material trends.

revenue_escalation.value: greater of SF Bay Area cost of living or California per capita personal income growth
revenue_escalation.source: Council Resolution No. 70,456-N.S. and the Measure FF ordinance, via City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12

net_effect_stated_by_city.value: a modest real increase in construction costs relative to available funding over the projection period
net_effect_stated_by_city.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12

software.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.8 (selection methods) and pp.11-12

ranking.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.8 (selection methods) and pp.11-12
ranking.note: WER ranks every street section and treatment option.

independent_model_status.purpose: Segment-level modelling would let BeTH project the condition distribution under each funding scenario, which the City does not publish. The current distribution is now held (PTAP-25); deterioration curves, treatment catalog and unit costs are not.

missing_inputs.needed_from: StreetSaver treatment catalog: eligibility PCI band, unit cost per square foot, service life, post-treatment PCI

independent_model_status.rule: No default, literature or assumed value is ever substituted for a missing input.

reconciliation_requirement: BeTH figures must reconcile to the City's adopted paving plan and StreetSaver output, with differences explained.
